comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: From round 1 (slot 2): muster-daemon passes cargo check and clippy -D warnings for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu (target added to the local toolchain) but has never run on Linux. Running its suite in the devenv container belongs here or right after.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: From round 2 (slot 1): muster-detect's Linux process probes (/proc stat, task children BFS, cmdline, environ) are type-checked for aarch64-linux-gnu but never run; run them live on the devenv with the daemon.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: From round 2 (slot 2): the gate links muster-daemon against the libghostty-vt dylib; a static daemon build (MUSTER_VT_LINK=static) needs its own cargo invocation in ./dev. Settle it here with the Linux builds (see also a_2XMtnSsUz).

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
MIP-3 section 12. No Muster artifact builds for Linux today, and remote panes need the daemon on the devenv.

Direction from the MIP: cross-compile from the Mac with the Zig 0.16 the build already requires, for `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` (added to `rust-toolchain.toml` targets); libghostty-vt built as a static library per target (`zig build -Demit-lib-vt -Dtarget=...`); link with `zig cc` or cargo-zigbuild; mimalloc instead of musl's allocator. herdr's release workflow does the equivalent on Linux runners, which is a reference for flags.

Also worth settling here: whether the default gate compile-checks the Linux targets (cheap insurance) or only `--ssh` and `--bundle` build them; and the binary size, which the MIP's case for bundling both Linux daemons in the app depends on.
title: Build muster-daemon for Linux x86_64 and aarch64
